title: How to Care for Your Baby Dragon
text:
Congratulations on your new baby dragon! Baby dragons are sweet, curious, and very {adjective}. Please read these instructions before you take yours home.

Feeding: Breakfast is a bowl of oatmeal with a {noun} on top. Lunch is a pile of {plural noun}. For dinner, most dragons like a plate of {food} with a little bit of ketchup. Sleeping: Baby dragons like to sleep curled up inside a {noun}. They snore {adverb} and puff tiny clouds of smoke. This is normal.

Playtime: Your dragon will want to {verb} every afternoon. Take it to the park and let it chase {plural noun}. If it starts {verb ending in ing}, that means it is happy. Warning: Baby dragons love to chew on {plural noun}, so keep yours on a high shelf.

Bath time: Dragons love bubbles! Fill the tub with warm water and add {number} rubber ducks. When your dragon is clean, it will shine like a {adjective} {noun}.

title: Pudding's First Day of Flying School
text:
Dear Diary, today was my first day at Flying School. I am only a small dragon, and my wings are still a little bit {adjective}. Mom packed me {food}, a {noun}, and a note that said, "You can do it!"

Our teacher, Mrs. Cloudberry, is the oldest dragon in the valley. She can fly {adverb} and do a loop around the moon. She told us to flap our wings {number} times and then jump off a soft, {adjective} hill.

My friend Toast went first. He {past tense verb} right into a pile of {plural noun}. Then it was my turn. I closed my eyes, flapped as hard as I could, and started {verb ending in ing}. When I opened my eyes, I was flying over {place}!

Tomorrow we will learn how to {verb} upside down. I am a little nervous, but Mrs. Cloudberry says every dragon feels nervous sometimes. She still gets nervous around {plural noun}. Good night, Diary. Love, Pudding the {adjective} Dragon

title: Help Wanted: Dragon Sitter
text:
HELP WANTED: Dragon sitter needed for Saturday afternoons. Our dragon, Mr. Biscuit, is big, green, and very {adjective}. He does not like to be left alone.

Your jobs will include brushing his scales with a {noun}, reading him stories about {plural noun}, and walking him around the lake. On the walk, he likes to stop and smell the {plural noun}. Please let him. Mr. Biscuit eats {number} sandwiches for lunch. He likes them cut into triangles with {food} in the middle. After lunch, he naps and hums {adverb} in his sleep.

Important: If Mr. Biscuit sneezes, step to the side. His sneezes are warm and smell like {food}. Also, please do not let him {verb} in the living room. Last week he {past tense verb} into the lamp, and now it leans to the left.

You must be good at {verb ending in ing} and not afraid of hugs. Pay is ten dollars and a {adjective} drawing of a {noun}.

title: A Dragon Opens a Bakery
text:
Big news from the village of Puddlebrook! A dragon named Marigold has opened a {adjective} bakery on Main Street. She bakes bread with her own warm breath, so she never needs an oven.

On opening day, the line went all the way to the {noun}. Marigold sold {number} loaves of bread before lunch. Her most popular treat is a {adjective} muffin with {plural noun} on top.

Customers say the bakery is cozy and smells like {food}. One boy said the cookies made him want to {verb}. A grandpa liked them so much that he {past tense verb} all the way home.

There have been a few small problems. Marigold is very tall, so she bakes while {verb ending in ing} on the floor. When she laughs, flour lands on people's {plural noun}. The bakery is closed on Mondays so Marigold can polish her {body part}. Please come early and talk {adverb}, because loud noises make her drop her {plural noun}.

title: Kids Ask a Dragon
text:
Welcome to Kids Talk, the radio show where kids ask the questions! Today our guest is Sparkle, a {adjective} dragon who lives on top of Blueberry Mountain. Ava, age six, asked, "What do you eat for breakfast?" Sparkle said, "Toast with {food} and a big glass of {plural noun}."

Leo asked, "Do dragons really keep treasure?" Sparkle laughed {adverb}. "Most dragons collect something," she said. "My uncle collects {plural noun}. I collect teacups. So far I have {number} cups, and my favorite one has a {noun} painted on it."

Mia asked, "What is the hardest part about being a dragon?" Sparkle {past tense verb} for a long time. "Sweaters," she said. "My wings make it very hard to {verb} in a sweater. Also, when I sneeze, my {body part} gets a little bit warm."

Last, the host asked Sparkle for some advice. "Be kind, eat your {plural noun}, and remember to {verb} before bed," she said. What a {adjective} guest!

title: You're Invited to Pip's Party
text:
You are invited to a birthday party! Pip the dragon is turning one hundred, which is very young for a dragon. The party is Saturday at two o'clock in the big cave behind Willow Hill. Look for the {adjective} balloons and the sign shaped like a {noun}.

There will be games, music, and a giant cake made of {plural noun}. Pip blows out candles very {adverb}, so please stand back. Last year he {past tense verb} so hard that the cake ended up on the ceiling. Please wear something {color}, because that is his favorite color.

For a gift, Pip would love a new toothbrush, a book about {plural noun}, or a {noun}. We will play Pin the Tail on the {animal} and a dancing game called Ready, Set, {verb}. Prizes go to whoever is best at {verb ending in ing}.

Please write back by Thursday so we know how many {plural noun} to make. Pip can't wait to {verb} with you!

title: Rules for the Dragon School Bus
text:
Good morning, students! This year our school bus is a friendly dragon named Gus. Gus is big and gentle, and he smells a little bit like {plural noun}. He flies {adverb} over the trees every morning. Please follow these rules.

Rule one: Hold on tight to the {adjective} handles on his back. Do not stand up, and do not try to {verb} while Gus is flying. Rule two: Gus is ticklish. Please do not touch his {body part}. The last time someone did, Gus {past tense verb} and we landed in a field full of {plural noun}.

Rule three: No snacks on the dragon. Crumbs fall between his scales, and he starts {verb ending in ing} and can't stop. Rule four: Say thank you when you get off. On Fridays, you may bring Gus a treat. His favorites are {food} and {plural noun}.

If you have questions, please ask the bus driver, Mr. Pine. He has been a bus driver for {number} years. He sits on a {noun} and wears a {adjective} helmet.

title: A Thank-You Letter from Bramble
text:
Dear Mrs. Henderson's First Grade Class, thank you so much for the get-well cards! I am feeling much better now. The doctor said I had a cold, and that is why every sneeze came out as {plural noun} instead of smoke.

Your cards are hanging on the wall of my cave. My favorite one has a drawing of me eating a {adjective} {noun}. Tommy, I love how you made my tail {color}. It looks very {adjective}.

I also want to thank you for the soup. It was warm and tasted like {food}. I ate it {adverb} with my biggest spoon. Then I took a long nap and {past tense verb} for {number} hours.

Next week, I will come visit your classroom. I promise to {verb} carefully and not knock over the bookshelf this time. At recess, we can practice {verb ending in ing} together. Please save me a seat by the {noun}.

Your friend,
Bramble the Dragon
P.S. I am bringing cookies shaped like {plural noun}.

title: Ember's First Report Card
text:
Dragon Valley School Report Card for Ember, Kindergarten. Reading: Ember is a {adjective} reader. He likes books about {plural noun} and reads them out loud. Sometimes he reads so {adverb} that the pages get a little warm.

Math: Ember can count to {number} on his claws. He is still learning to share his {plural noun}. Yesterday he hid all the counting blocks under his {noun}. Art: Ember's painting of a {noun} is hanging in the front hall. It is only a little bit smoky.

Music: Ember loves to {verb} during music time. His singing voice is very {adjective}. Please practice {verb ending in ing} quietly at home.

Behavior: Ember is kind to the class {animal} and always helps clean up. On Tuesday, he blew all the leaves into one big pile and then {past tense verb} right in the middle of it. Great job, Ember! Keep being {adjective}!

title: Grandma Dragon's Famous Soup
text:
This is the soup that Grandma Dragon makes every winter. She says it warms your tummy and makes your scales {adjective}. You will need a grown-up to help.

First, fill a big pot with water and add two carrots, one onion, and a handful of {plural noun}. Grandma Dragon does not use a stove. She just breathes on the pot {adverb} until it bubbles.

Next, add a spoonful of {food} and stir it with a {noun}. You must stir {number} times to the left, or the soup will taste {adjective}. While the soup cooks, it is very important to {verb}. Grandma does this every time, usually while {verb ending in ing}.

When the soup is ready, pour it into a {adjective} bowl and put a {noun} on top. Blow on it before you eat it, unless you are a dragon. Grandma's neighbor once {past tense verb} for joy after one sip. Enjoy, and save some for the {plural noun}!
